done_when: no test creates, names or archives a thread in the user's real Codex home: every test that reaches Codex uses a throwaway Codex home, and a test run leaves the real home's thread list unchanged, proven by an end-to-end test

findings.body: The snapshots surround only this test's isolated `forge ask` invocation, not a test run. Removing `isolated_codex_home` from the smoke test would restore the original thread pollution while this test could still pass: its own isolation remains intact, and smoke-test mutations can occur outside this snapshot window. Exercise the actual conversation-producing tests inside the before/after check so the regression proof fails when their isolation breaks.
findings.title: Not done: a test run leaves the real home's thread list unchanged, proven by an end-to-end test

findings.body: This guard skips the new test on the normal CI runner: `.github/workflows/forge.yml:19–21` runs pytest without installing Forge's real SDK. The workflow that does install and authenticate that SDK runs only `tests/test_codex_smoke.py` (`.github/workflows/codex-smoke.yml:29–38`), excluding this new file. Consequently, neither workflow executes the required end-to-end isolation proof. Include it in a configured test job where its prerequisites are present.
findings.title: Not done: run the Codex-home end-to-end regression test in CI

findings.body: For users whose login lives under a custom `CODEX_HOME`, this unconditional copy now fails with `FileNotFoundError` when `~/.codex/auth.json` is absent, or copies credentials from a different account when it exists. Forge already honors the configured home (`src/forge/worker.py:120`). Capture that home before the fixture overrides the environment and use it for authentication and the real-home snapshots; the new regression test hardcodes the same incorrect location.
findings.title: Read authentication from the original configured Codex home

why: Forge's test suite starts real Codex conversations in the user's own Codex home, so every test run leaves new threads in their Codex chat list
